answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to keep a live thread of presence: each week it must complete a fresh, timed task in a one-to-one session with a randomly chosen established peer, and missed weeks dissolve its standing the way water hollows karst. Because sessions overlap and peers rotate, running ten fakes means staffing ten simultaneous conversations, a canyon of ongoing attention no script can widen cheaply, so cost grows with every extra identity.
